  WHY: Short or non-token-shaped secret values can appear in stderr diagnostics and workflow logs; all six reviewers agree on severity.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "the values of secret-named env vars (a multiline value line by line; a value or line under 8 characters only where it stands as a whole word) are masked before security_audit_sanitize_log_value"

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/security_audit.sh: `security_audit_mask_stderr_line`, the `case "${secret_env_name}" in` statement matching `*TOKEN*|*API_KEY*|*SECRET*|*PASSWORD*|PAT|*_PAT|PAT_*|*_PAT_*)` | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Bash `case` glob patterns are case-sensitive, so lowercase or mixed-case secret environment variable names fall through to `*) continue` and their values are never masked.
  WHY: If a runner exports a lowercase-named secret variable and Codex echoes its value to stderr, a short or non-standard-format value can appear unmasked in `captured_path_error=` and `codex-stderr-tail` output.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- scripts/security_audit.sh: lines 122-128 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The case statement matching secret-named environment variables is case-sensitive, so lowercase or mixed-case names fail to match and are skipped.
  WHY: A short value not caught by generic token masks can be printed in plaintext in `captured_path_error=` and `codex-stderr-tail` workflow log lines.
- Requirement: "the values of secret-named env vars (a multiline value line by line; a value or line under 8 characters only where it stands as a whole word) are masked before security_audit_sanitize_log_value"
  Expected change site: scripts/security_audit.sh in security_audit_mask_stderr_line and tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py
  Evidence of absence: scripts/security_audit.sh line 124 matches secret_env_name directly against uppercase-only patterns (*TOKEN*|*API_KEY*|*SECRET*|*PASSWORD*, etc.) without case normalization, leaving lowercase and mixed-case secret-named environment variables unmasked. Additionally, tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py only exercises uppercase variable names (SHORT_API_KEY, MULTILINE_SECRET) and lacks regression coverage asserting that lowercase or mixed-case secret environment variable values are redacted from emitted output.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/security_audit.sh: `security_audit_mask_stderr_line`, the case-statement matching `secret_env_name` (`*TOKEN*|*API_KEY*|*SECRET*|*PASSWORD*|PAT|*_PAT|PAT_*|*_PAT_*`) at the top of the while loop over `compgen -e` (added in the round-6 hunk) | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Bash `case` pattern matching is case-sensitive, so lowercase or mixed-case secret-named environment variables fall through to `*) continue` and their values are never read by the masking loop.
  WHY: Short or non-token-shaped values can reach `security_audit_sanitize_log_value` and the workflow log unchanged, including in `codex-stderr-tail line=` entries and `security-audit: captured_path_error=` diagnostics.
- Requirement: "Every line is masked for sk- keys, long hex and base64 runs (standard or URL-safe, padded or not), and the values of secret-named env vars (short values where they stand as a whole word), then passed through the existing log sanitizer" (PR description checklist item 3, `agents.md` §7 note, `changelog.d/5785-security-audit-codex-stderr-tail.md`). The PR description and the Copilot review comment `4154966986` make the guarantee case-independent.
  Expected change site: `tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py` alongside `test_security_audit_codex_stderr_tail_masks_short_secrets_and_unpadded_base64` and `test_security_audit_codex_failure_prints_masked_stderr_tail_with_provider_402`.
  Evidence of absence: Every existing fixture sets an uppercase-named env var (`SHORT_API_KEY`, `MULTILINE_SECRET`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `test-openrouter-key`, `test-token`). No test sets a lowercase or mixed-case name such as `api_key` or `client_secret` and asserts the value is absent from the emitted stderr tail or from `captured_path_error=`. The fix to `security_audit_mask_stderr_line` therefore has no automated coverage; a regression on case handling would not be caught by the contract tests.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/security_audit.sh: security_audit_mask_stderr_line(), the case statement matching secret_env_name | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Secret-name detection is case-sensitive, so lowercase or mixed-case names such as api_key and client_secret are skipped.
  WHY: If Codex writes a short, non-token-shaped value from one of those exported variables to stderr, it is not redacted by the generic token masks and can appear in failure diagnostics.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- scripts/security_audit.sh: security_audit_mask_stderr_line, the `case "${secret_env_name}" in` statement at line 98 (round 6 hunk), specifically the pattern `*TOKEN*|*API_KEY*|*SECRET*|*PASSWORD*|PAT|*_PAT|PAT_*|*_PAT_*` | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The case patterns are case-sensitive bash globs, so lowercase or mixed-case secret-named environment variables fall through to `*) continue` and their values are never masked.
  WHY: If Codex echoes a short non-token-shaped value to stderr, it can leak into the Actions log; the test suite only exercises uppercase names.
- Requirement: "the values of secret-named env vars (a multiline value line by line; a value or line under 8 characters only where it stands as a whole word) are masked before security_audit_sanitize_log_value" (agents.md note at line 2175, changelog.d/5785-security-audit-codex-stderr-tail.md line 5, PR description checklist item 3)
  Expected change site: scripts/security_audit.sh in security_audit_mask_stderr_line (line 98, the case statement); tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py
  Evidence of absence: scripts/security_audit.sh line 98 matches secret_env_name directly against uppercase patterns without case normalization, so lowercase and mixed-case secret-named environment variables are not matched and their values are not masked. tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py only includes fixtures with uppercase names and lacks any regression test asserting that lowercase or mixed-case secret environment variable values are redacted from emitted output.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- scripts/security_audit.sh: security_audit_mask_stderr_line, the `case "${secret_env_name}" in` statement (diff lines ~124-130) | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The case patterns that gate secret-name detection are case-sensitive, so lowercase or mixed-case exported environment variables do not match and their values are never extracted or masked.
  WHY: A short non-token-shaped secret can pass through entirely to the GitHub Actions log in `codex-stderr-tail` lines and the `captured_path_error=` diagnostic.
- Requirement: "the values of secret-named env vars (a multiline value line by line; a value or line under 8 characters only where it stands as a whole word) are masked before security_audit_sanitize_log_value" (agents.md note at line 2175, changelog.d/5785-security-audit-codex-stderr-tail.md line 5, PR description checklist item 3) — no case qualification stated.
  Expected change site: scripts/security_audit.sh in `security_audit_mask_stderr_line`, the `case "${secret_env_name}" in` statement; tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py for a lowercase/mixed-case regression test.
  Evidence of absence: The `case` statement matches `secret_env_name` directly against uppercase-only glob patterns without case normalization (e.g. `"${secret_env_name^^}"`). Lowercase and mixed-case secret-named env vars (`api_key`, `client_secret`, `auth_token`, `db_password`) fall through to `*) continue` and their values are never masked. All existing test fixtures use uppercase names only (`SHORT_API_KEY`, `MULTILINE_SECRET`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`); no test asserts redaction for a lowercase or mixed-case secret-named env var. Copilot review comment entry[37] (id 4154966986) independently identified this defect.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
